This release adds an optional MCP server, so your users can connect AI apps like Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor
to their account, along with a new way to define AI tools once and share them between MCP and your in-app agents.

### MCP server

Pegasus can now include an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server, built on
[django-mcpz](https://pypi.org/project/django-mcpz/). Enable it with the new "Use MCP Server" option.

- **Users connect MCP clients with OAuth.** Clients add your site's `/mcp` URL as a connector, and users approve
  access on an authorization page in your app.
- **Added a "Connected AI Apps" section to the profile page.** It shows the MCP server URL and lists the
  connected apps, each of which can be disconnected.
- **Connected apps are disconnected automatically** when a user changes their password or 2FA setup.
- Added a daily Celery task that clears expired OAuth codes and tokens.

### App tools

- **Added "app tools": AI tools defined once and shared by MCP and the in-app agents.** A tool is a function that
  takes the user and an optional pydantic model of parameters. See `apps/utils/app_tools.py`.
- Added tools to read and update the user's profile. The weather and admin agents now use them, and the MCP server
  serves them when it's enabled.

### Upgrading

If you enable the MCP server, make sure requests to `/.well-known/` reach Django.
MCP clients use discovery documents at those paths to find your OAuth endpoints.
Some server setups (often from Let's Encrypt/certbot instructions) serve all of `/.well-known/` from a directory on disk,
which makes these return a 404 and prevents clients from connecting.
If that's the case, narrow the rule to only the paths that need it, e.g. `/.well-known/acme-challenge/`.
